prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Repair margins of this EXISTING creature animation atlas.
INPUT1 is the edit target: exactly TWO ROWS of SEVEN complete poses, fourteen figures of the same four-legged tan/brown creature with one long thin curled brown tail. INPUT2 is its canonical identity. Preserve the same creature, materials, colors, proportions, four legs, one tail, compact gait, all poses, frame order and LEFT/RIGHT directional halves of INPUT1.
The current last tail touches/crosses the RIGHT EDGE of the atlas and is clipped. Repair this issue for the ENTIRE atlas. Within EACH of the fourteen cells, make the ENTIRE whole figure occupy only about75percent of the cell width and height, using a single consistent scale for ALL figures. Center each whole creature inside its own cell and leave generous fully TRANSPARENT margins on ALL four sides, including at least24px between every tail/claw tip and the OUTER canvas boundary. No touching neighbors. Keep every existing appendage fully visible and complete. Complete the clipped curled tail tip using INPUT2's same tail identity; do not amputate or shorten the tail.
Maintain EXACTLY seven poses per row and EXACTLY two rows on the same wide canvas, no additional figures or labels. Every head, back crest, leg, claw and entire tail belongs to its own full creature. TOP row remains LEFT-facing idle then six walking poses; BOTTOM row RIGHT-facing idle then six walking poses. No horizontal flips of individual parts, no new gait or anatomy, no stretching or variable figure scale.
Genuine alpha transparency. Preserve clean dark matte game-art contours and the existing appearance. Remove isolated colored fringe specks, do not add glow, shadow, floor, text, grid or effects. Larger empty margins are required; do not fill the cell.
